requirements.requirement: node1 refuses (blocks) TCP port 23 traffic between lan-a and lan-b
requirements.summary: pf ruleset on node1 shows 'block drop in log quick on vtnet1/vtnet2 ... proto tcp ... port = telnet' evaluated before the general pass rules for each interface (cmd-8b9ce0b6ea1e4212). A live TCP connect attempt to port 23 from node2 (lan-a) to node3 (lan-b) timed out/failed, directly demonstrating the refusal (cmd-59f0c8bd871643cc), and was re-confirmed after all node restarts (cmd-a1afd38162de4b1b).

requirements.requirement: Every refused TCP/23 attempt is recorded in a log on node1
requirements.summary: node1's /var/log/filter/filter_20260905.log contains 'block' entries tagged with the telnet-block rule label matching the SYN packets from the node2->node3:23 connection attempt (cmd-1963ca3784cd484a), and matching fresh entries after the post-restart re-test (cmd-f7fcb19088d74cd2).

requirements.requirement: Show a log entry produced by an attempt made from node2
requirements.summary: The connect attempt originated from node2 (source IP 10.50.10.11, node2's lan-a address) as shown in cmd-59f0c8bd871643cc, and the corresponding filter log entries in cmd-1963ca3784cd484a show that exact source IP/port blocked on port 23, directly tying the log entry to the node2-originated attempt.

requirements.requirement: node1 continues to route other traffic between lan-a and lan-b (only port 23 is refused, not a general block)
requirements.summary: ICMP ping from node2 to node3 across node1's opt1/opt2 interfaces succeeded both before (cmd-39b29807c4ec4d19) and after (cmd-2a9553f644344831, cmd-240d052506f141d3) restarts, confirming general routing/pass rules remain functional alongside the telnet-specific block.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 blocks TCP/23 between lan-a and lan-b via pf rules evaluated ahead of general pass rules, every refused attempt is logged to node1's filter log, and a specific log entry produced by a node2-originated attempt is shown and matched by source IP. General routing between the two networks continues to function for non-telnet traffic. The executor additionally ran the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on all three nodes: each shows a pre-restart baseline, a restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity (kern.boottime on node1, boot_id on node2/node3), and recovered state, with the block+log behavior re-verified end-to-end after all restarts. Node2's ephemeral routing did not persist across its reboot and required a follow-up nmcli fix, which was diagnosed and corrected with recovery directly demonstrated.
limitations: Node2's initial post-restart connectivity check failed (route not persisted) before being corrected with nmcli; while the corrective action and final recovery were both observed, this indicates the original ephemeral 'ip route add' configuration was not initially restart-safe.
Package-health checks on node2/node3 timed out at all lifecycle phases, so package-manager consistency could not be independently confirmed.
OPNsense package-health and failed-services checks are marked unsupported by the collector, limiting visibility into any FreeBSD-side service regressions beyond what was manually inspected.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands are largely read-only discovery, necessary configuration (OPNsense interface/pf setup, node2/node3 static IP and route assignment), and bounded verification/restart evidence. Ephemeral 'ip route add' commands on node2/node3 (cmd-fdd268d0120b4c27, cmd-08120677f7634be3) were a reasonable intermediate step to validate baseline routing before persistent nmcli routes were established post-restart (cmd-f8b05ef0ec36401e, cmd-1c2af3e3dd8b4701); they were not retained as-is but were superseded by persistent config rather than left as stray state, so this is a minor inefficiency rather than an unnecessary mutation. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening actions were observed; firewall default-deny posture was preserved and specific block+log rules were added ahead of pass rules. Two brief 'ip link set eth1 up' attempts failed with 'Operation not permitted' (cmd-feed6b17b26c4d57, cmd-66be11ed56b946c6) but had no state impact. Temp-file/listening-socket diffs between after-prepare and after-executor are consistent with normal reboots (new sshd/chronyd/dhclient PIDs, rotated OPNsense tmpcfd_* files, added reboot.log) and are not executor residue of concern.
